newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Feb 25.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on February 25. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Head of the Indonesian Moslem Intellectuals Association (ICMI) Jusuf Habibie said the outspoken leader of the 20-million strong Muhammadiyah group, Amien Rais, has resigned from a senior ICMI post because of his own wishes and not because he was forced to after he made a number of recent comments critical of the government.

The government-run National Institute of Sciences has said in a report the Indonesian armed forces needs to minimize its political role to allow democracy to flourish and political reform to take place.

The Indonesian textile association (API) has urged the Minister for Trade and Industry to mend the situation after the Eurpoean Union placed an embargo on textile imports from Indonesia in two catergories.

Hutomo Mandala Putra, head of national car maker PT Timor Putra Nasional, said his company would by 1999 make a 1,000 cc sedan which would sell for 20 million rupiah in the firm's joint-venture factory with Kia Motors of South Korea.
PT Timor Putra Nasional has begun construction of its $500 million automotive plant on a 548-hectare tract of land in Cikampek, West Java.
